title: Traffic Targeting & Fallback Interaction Notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of interaction patterns and micro-wireframes for traffic targeting controls in the Rollouts console. Focus is on three flows: staged canary (percentage ramps), A/B traffic splits, and automatic fallback policies (graceful downgrade to cheaper/backup model). This is a working doc for product+design+eng sync; expect iteration.

High-level UX goals:
- Make traffic targeting concise: primary control should answer ‘who gets what’ in one glance.
- Surface safety & metrics early: when editing a rollout, show the recent latency/error delta for candidate models and the projected cost impact.
- Make fallback policies explicit and testable: preview the fallback chain and simulate a failure.
- Avoid heavy modal nesting: prefer inline expanders and a single right rail for live preview and metrics.

User journeys (short):
1) Small startup wants a canary: set 5% traffic to new model for 24h, auto ramp to 50% if error rate delta < 0.5% and latency < 50ms extra, otherwise rollback to previous stable model.
2) Product team running A/B: split 60/40 between model-v1 (baseline) and model-v2, collect prompt-level quality scores, and run for 48h. If model-v2 shows quality regressions > threshold, automatically route 100% to baseline and notify.
3) Enterprise customer needs fallback chain: primary heavy model -> quantized cheaper variant -> small embed-only model for non-critical routes. On GPU OOM or high queue depth, automatically promote to fallback.

Wireframe annotations (right-rail + inline sections):
- Top: rollout title, environment selector (hosted/dedicated/private), status pill (Draft / Running / Paused).
- Primary canvas: visual traffic dial (pie + percentage sliders). Each segment is clickable and expands a side card with model details, recent metrics, and rollout rules.
- Right rail: live preview (sample prompts + responses), health strip (latency p50/p95, error rate, queue depth), cost delta estimate (per-1M tokens), and preview simulation controls.

Micro-interactions and edge cases:
- Editing percentages: typing vs drag slider. If typing causes total >100% show inline suggestion button ‘normalize automatically’ and highlight segments that changed.
- Overlapping rules: if a rule targets the same user cohort (eg: email domain) warn with a yellow banner and show winner-takes precedence rule ordering. Allow drag-to-reorder rules.
- Simulate failure: a compact menu in the right rail lets you 'simulate latency spike' or 'simulate 500 errors' for N minutes and shows what fallback would occur and the expected RPS impact.
- Locking & approvals: for enterprise environments, editing controls are disabled behind ‘requires approval’ with a clear CTA to request approval (creates ticket link).

Automatic fallback policy UI:
- Represent fallback chains as an ordered list with small cards: [Primary model] -> [Fallback 1 - quantized] -> [Fallback 2 - small model] -> [Last resort: 503].
- Each link shows trigger conditions (OOM, error-rate > X, p95 latency > Y, queue depth > Z) and a test button.
- Default policy presets: Low-risk (aggressive fallback), Balanced (recommended), Cost-first (fall back to cheaper sooner). These presets should be editable.

Observability surfaces to include in the console while editing rollouts:
- Rolling window comparison: show delta metrics between candidate and baseline for p50/p95 latency, token cost, error types, and quality evals (if linked).
- Traffic heatmap: by region and route, to help decide safe canary size.
- Incident preview: if a fallback would route >30% traffic to a cheaper model, warn with potential SLA impact.

Acceptance criteria for initial implementation (MVP scope):
- Users can create a staged rollout with percentage-based segments and save as Draft.
- UI shows p50/p95 latency and error rate for each segment (pulls from telemetry).
- Fallback chain can be defined with at least 2 fallback targets and attach trigger conditions.
- Simulation controls allow testing latency/error triggers and display which fallback would activate.
- Changes to live rollouts require an explicit confirm modal summarizing impacted routes and cost delta.

Backlog / next steps (short bullets):
- [ ] Implement right-rail skeleton with sample prompts + health strip (ENG: console/frontend).
- [ ] Telemetry API endpoint for per-model p95/p50 & error breakdown (ENG: infra/observability).
- [ ] Wire up presets for fallback policies and make editable (PRODUCT + DESIGN).
- [ ] Add normalization helper for percentage edits and conflict resolution UI (DESIGN).
- [ ] E2E test plan for simulate-failure scenarios (SRE + QA).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How many presets? Start with 3 to avoid complexity.
- Should fallback triggers support compound conditions (eg: p95>Y AND error_rate>Z)? MVP: single condition, with future support for boolean expressions.
- Rollback vs fallback naming confusion: users conflate 'rollback' (manual revert) with 'fallback' (automatic alternative). Need copy clarity in UI.
- Cost estimations can be noisy; show confidence bands and how estimate is computed (sampled tokens * model price).

Short example copy snippets for UI strings (for localization prep):
- Segment card header: "5% — model-v2 (canary)"
- Fallback chain label: "Automatic fallback sequence"
- Simulation CTA: "Simulate 5m latency spike"
- Confirmation modal summary title: "Confirm rollout change: affects 3 routes — projected +$120/month"

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc focuses on interactions; separate doc will specify GraphQL payload shapes and permissions.
- Design sketches below are rough and meant to prompt discussion in Tues sync.

Rough ASCII sketch (primary canvas):
[Rollout title]   [Environment selector]   [Status pill]
-------------------------------------------------------
|  Traffic pie  |  Segment list (click to expand)     |
|  (interactive) |  - model-v2: 5%  [edit] [metrics]   |
|                |  - model-v1: 95% [baseline]           |
-------------------------------------------------------
| Right rail: Live preview | Health: p50/p95 | Cost delta |
| [sample prompt] -> [response]   | p50: 45ms | +12%       |

-- end --
